mainTopic: Which services need the right hand: reading 'finger' in a פסוק, and the rule of אצבע and כהונה
overview: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree about whether the word 'finger' in a פסוק describes only the words after it or the words on both sides. אביי shows that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון takes a third approach: 'finger' describes only the words right before it. Next, רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: where the תורה says אצבע and כהונה, the right hand is required. After a first guess that both words are needed fails because of קמיצה, רבא explains that either word is enough. That rule is then limited to acts that hold back כפרה, like the מצורע. The גמרא shows that רבי שמעון holds that אצבע works alone but כהונה needs אצבע, and a ברייתא confirms that he allows קבלה and זריקה with the left hand. Finally, רבא's יד–יד link for קמיצה is shown to be needed, because one source covers taking the קומץ and the other covers placing it in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: reading a verse forward and backward
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree about whether a word in a פסוק connects to what comes before it as well as what comes after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about whether a verse is explained using what comes before it and after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the earlier argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is really about. It comes down to how you read a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק 'the כהן shall take of the blood with his finger and put it', the word 'finger' sits between 'take' and 'put'. רבי שמעון connects it only to what follows (putting the blood). The רבנן connect it to both sides, so both taking and putting need the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse in the תורה
Is explained or expounded
With what comes before it and what comes after it
They disagree

phrases.english: About whether a verse is explained with what comes before it and after it
phrases.notes: The verse is the one with 'finger' between 'take' and 'put'. The question is which of those two words 'finger' goes with.

phrases.english: they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about what רבי שמעון and the רבנן are arguing about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether a word in a פסוק connects to the words before it, the words after it, or both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading rule decides whether using the left hand in קבלה disqualifies the קרבן.

steps.title: אביי: a third opinion that differs from both sides
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees with both his father and the רבנן. He brings a ברייתא where the hand rule applies only to the act the 'finger' is written about.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון departs from his father's view and from the רבנן. A ברייתא teaches that wherever 'finger' is written about קבלה, using the wrong hand in קבלה disqualifies, but in נתינה it is still kosher. Wherever 'finger' is written about נתינה, using the wrong hand in נתינה disqualifies, but in קבלה it is still kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי introduces a third view and quotes a ברייתא to show it. According to this view, the right-hand rule applies only to the specific act the word 'finger' is attached to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father, רבי שמעון, links 'finger' to what follows. The רבנן link it to both sides. רבי אלעזר allows for a case where 'finger' applies to נתינה only, which is a different reading from both of them (explained in the next steps).

keyTerms.meaning: Departs from, disagrees with
Finger, which hints that the right hand is required
Collecting the blood in a vessel
Placing the blood on the מזבח
He changed, meaning he did it the wrong way (with the left hand)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This view of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
goes out from his father's view,
phrases.notes: His father is רבי שמעון from the step before.

phrases.english: and goes out from the Rabbis' view.
As it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
Any place where 'finger' is said about collecting,
if he changed in the collecting, it is disqualified;
if he changed in the placing, it is valid.
And any place where 'finger' is said about placing,
if he changed in the placing, it is disqualified;
if he changed in the collecting, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַפְּקָא מִדַּאֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the two-sided dispute just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right-hand requirement applies only to the act that 'finger' is written about. Using the wrong hand for the other act does not disqualify.

steps.title: Where is 'finger' written only about placing the blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תורה writes 'finger' only about נתינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is 'finger' said about placing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. It wants to find the פסוק where 'finger' goes only with placing the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under both רבי שמעון's reading and the רבנן's reading, 'finger' always includes placing. So we need to see which פסוק gives רבי אלעזר a case of 'finger' that applies to נתינה alone, and why.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?

phrases.english: And where is 'finger' said about placing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק writes 'finger' only about placing, and what reading rule makes it so.

steps.title: The verse about the bull, and רבי אלעזר's reading rule
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'take of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the מזבח with your finger'. Because רבי אלעזר links a word only to what comes right before it, 'finger' goes only with placing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall take of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger.' He holds that a verse is explained using what is right before it, but not what is before that, and not what comes after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the פסוק and explains how רבי אלעזר reads it. 'With your finger' comes right after 'put it', so it describes only the putting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Take' is two steps back (לפני פניו), so 'finger' does not reach it. רבי שמעון reads forward and the רבנן read in both directions. רבי אלעזר reads only one step back, so his view really is different from both, just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes before the words right before it, meaning two steps back
He holds, this is his opinion
The corners ('horns') of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to read 'finger': רבי שמעון links it to what follows, the רבנן link it to both sides, and רבי אלעזר links it only to what comes immediately before.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And you shall take of the blood of the bull
and put it on the corners of the altar with your finger.'
And he holds: a verse is explained with what is right before it,
and not with what is before that, and not with what is after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is שמות 29:12, read with the rule that a word connects only to the phrase right before it.

steps.title: 'Finger' and 'priesthood' always mean the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that wherever the תורה mentions אצבע and כהונה, the act must be done with the right hand. The next steps work out whether he means both words together or either one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Any place where 'finger' and 'priesthood' is said, it means only the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a general rule from רבי יוחנן. The words 'finger' and 'priesthood' in the תורה are signals that the right hand is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a wider rule than the specific פסוקים discussed above. The wording 'אצבע and כהונה' leaves a question that the next steps take up: does the פסוק need both words, or is one enough?

keyTerms.meaning: Priesthood, the mention of the כהן
The right hand
It is nothing but, it means only

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Any place where 'finger' and 'priesthood' is said,
it means only the right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֶצְבַּע וּכְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section with a general rule about the right hand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever 'finger' and 'priesthood' appear, the service must be done with the right hand. Whether both are needed or either one is enough is worked out in steps 6–8.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the basis for the next discussion about which services require the right hand.

steps.title: First guess: the right hand is needed only when both words appear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first thinks רבי יוחנן means you need both אצבע and כהונה in the פסוק. The example is the blood of the חטאת, learned from מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: We first thought both words are needed. For example, the פסוק says 'the כהן shall take of the blood of the חטאת with his finger', and we learn from מצורע, where it says 'his right finger', that this finger is the right one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first way to understand רבי יוחנן's rule. This is setting up the next move, where this reading will be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the right hand is needed only when a פסוק mentions both אצבע and כהונה together. The חטאת פסוק has both words, and the word 'right' is borrowed from the מצורע פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: It entered our mind (a first guess that will be rejected)
We need both
A person with צרעת, whose purification uses the kohen's right finger
And he learns it (from another פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a first guess. Don't take it as the final meaning of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It entered our mind that we need both,
as it is written: 'And the kohen shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25. Both כהן and 'finger' are in this פסוק.

phrases.english: and he learns it from the מצורע,
as it is written: 'And the kohen shall dip his right finger'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a first reading of רבי יוחנן's rule from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First guess: the right hand is required only when the פסוק says both אצבע and כהונה.

steps.title: קמיצה proves one word is enough
steps.stepSummary: קמיצה only mentions כהונה, yet a משנה says doing it with the left hand is פסול. So 'both' cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at קמיצה. Only כהונה is written there, and still the משנה says that if he took the handful with his left hand, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'both words' reading with a case where only one word appears, yet the right hand is still required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both words were needed, קמיצה with the left hand should be fine, since only כהונה is mentioned. The משנה says it is פסול, so the first guess fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a handful from a מנחה
With the left hand
Disqualified

phrases.english: But there is the taking of the handful,
where only the priesthood is written,
and we learned: if he took the handful with the left, it is disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disproves the first guess of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that both אצבע and כהונה are needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קמיצה has only כהונה, yet the left hand makes it פסול, so one word must be enough.

steps.title: רבא: either word is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יוחנן means either אצבע or כהונה is enough to require the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא says: it means either finger or priesthood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new reading of רבי יוחנן's rule to fit the case of קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now one word alone, either אצבע or כהונה, is enough to require the right hand. This fits קמיצה, where only כהונה is written.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier idea)
Either… or

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אוֹ אֶצְבַּע, אוֹ כְּהוּנָּה.
phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: either finger or priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading after the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both אצבע and כהונה must appear.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either word alone requires the right hand.

steps.title: אביי: carrying limbs to the ramp says כהונה but uses the left hand
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that carrying the limbs to the ramp has כהונה in its פסוק, yet the משנה says the right leg is carried in the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: carrying the limbs to the ramp has כהונה written about it, 'And the כהן shall bring all of it and burn it on the altar', and the Master said this refers to carrying limbs to the ramp. Yet we learned: the right leg is in his left hand, with the skin side facing out!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's 'either word' rule with a case where כהונה is written, yet the left hand is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כהונה alone requires the right hand, carrying limbs to the ramp should need the right hand. But the משנה describes a כהן carrying a limb in his left hand, so רבא's rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the limbs of the קרבן to the ramp of the מזבח
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The skin side of the limb

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵי הוֹלָכַת אֵבָרִים לַכֶּבֶשׁ –
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: But there is carrying the limbs to the ramp,
where priesthood is written about them,
as it is written: 'And the kohen shall bring all of it and burn it on the altar';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:13. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר: זוֹ הוֹלָכַת אֵבָרִים לַכֶּבֶשׁ;
phrases.english: and the Master said: this is carrying the limbs to the ramp;
and we learned: the right leg is in his left hand,
and its skin side faces outward!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אביי הרי הולכת אברים לכבש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that either אצבע or כהונה requires the right hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying limbs mentions כהונה, yet the משנה has the כהן use his left hand.

steps.title: The rule applies only to acts that hold back atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'either אצבע or כהונה' applies only to an act that holds back the כפרה, like the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we say 'either finger or priesthood', that is only for something that holds back atonement, like the מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by narrowing רבא's rule to acts that are needed for the כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right hand is learned from מצורע, where the act is needed for the purification. So the rule only covers similar acts that hold back כפרה. Carrying limbs to the ramp does not hold back כפרה, so the left hand is fine there.

keyTerms.meaning: An act that holds back atonement if not done
Similar to
When we say

steps.whatToRemember: The right hand is required when the פסוק says either אצבע or כהונה, but only for acts that hold back כפרה, like the מצורע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the final limits of רבי יוחנן's right-hand rule. That is why carrying limbs can be done with the left hand.

phrases.english: When we say either finger or priesthood,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: that is for something that holds back atonement,
similar to the מצורע.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי אמרינן או אצבע או כהונה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 9 by narrowing רבא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any act with אצבע or כהונה needs the right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only acts that hold back כפרה, like the מצורע, need the right hand.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'either אצבע or כהונה' rule covers only acts that hold back כפרה.

steps.title: Collecting the blood seems to break the rule
steps.stepSummary: קבלה has כהונה in its פסוק and holds back the כפרה, yet רבי שמעון in the משנה allows collecting the blood with the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about collecting the blood? כהונה is written about it, and it is an act that holds back the כפרה. Yet we learned in a משנה: if he collected the blood with his left hand, it is פסול, and רבי שמעון says it is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to the rule from Step 10. It points to קבלה, where רבי שמעון allows the left hand even though the case seems to fit the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said: if a פסוק mentions אצבע or כהונה, and the act holds back the כפרה, the right hand is required. קבלה meets both conditions, since it has כהונה and it holds back the כפרה. So how can רבי שמעון allow the left hand?

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the blood of a קרבן in a כלי שרת
An act that holds back the כפרה, so without it there is no atonement
The left hand
Rules it valid (כשר)

phrases.english: But what about collecting the blood, about which כהונה is written,
and it is an act that holds back the כפרה;
and we learned: if he collected with the left hand, it is פסול,
and רבי שמעון rules it valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the narrowed rule from Step 10 against a case that seems to meet every condition.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that either אצבע or כהונה requires the right hand when the act holds back the כפרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קבלה has כהונה and holds back the כפרה, yet רבי שמעון allows the left hand.

steps.title: רבי שמעון needs both words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון only requires the right hand when the פסוק has both אצבע and כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון requires both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that רבי שמעון holds a stricter version of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, כהונה alone is not enough. The פסוק must mention both אצבע and כהונה before the right hand is required. קבלה only has כהונה, so the left hand is כשר according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, meaning both words (אצבע and כהונה)
Requires

phrases.english: רבי שמעון requires both.
phrases.notes: "Both" means the פסוק must mention אצבע and also כהונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by giving רבי שמעון his own stricter version of the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting opinions: the 'either one' rule belongs to the תנא קמא, and רבי שמעון needs both.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that either אצבע or כהונה is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון requires both words before the right hand is required.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון treats אצבע alone as enough
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון saying that wherever יד or אצבע appears, it means the right hand. That suggests one word is enough for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really require both? But it was taught in a ברייתא that רבי שמעון says: wherever 'hand' is written, it means only the right hand, and 'finger' means only the right hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 12 with a ברייתא in רבי שמעון's own name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון says that the word אצבע by itself means the right hand. He says nothing about also needing כהונה. That goes against the claim that he needs both words.

keyTerms.meaning: Hand
The right hand
Finger

phrases.english: Does רבי שמעון really require both?!
But it was taught in a ברייתא, רבי שמעון says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יָד – אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יָמִין,
phrases.english: Wherever "hand" is said, it means only the right hand,
and "finger" means only the right hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 12 using a ברייתא in רבי שמעון's name.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון requires both אצבע and כהונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון says that אצבע alone means the right hand, so he does not need both words.

steps.title: אצבע works alone, כהונה does not
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון, אצבע by itself requires the right hand. כהונה only requires the right hand when אצבע is also in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אצבע does not need כהונה, but כהונה needs אצבע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by explaining exactly what 'both' meant for רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words do not have equal power. אצבע is strong enough to require the right hand by itself, which matches the ברייתא. כהונה is weaker and needs אצבע alongside it, so קבלה, which only has כהונה, is כשר with the left hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not need

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון: אצבע alone means the right hand. כהונה alone does not, which is why he allows קבלה with the left hand.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 12's 'both' does not mean each word is useless alone. It only means that כהונה cannot work without אצבע.

phrases.english: "Finger" does not need "priesthood,"
"priesthood" needs "finger."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by refining the meaning of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refinement: the two words are given unequal weight.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון needs both words in every case, which contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אצבע alone is enough. כהונה works only together with אצבע.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק mention a כהן by collecting the blood?
steps.stepSummary: If כהונה alone does not require the right hand for רבי שמעון, the extra mention of כהן by קבלה seems to have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'כהן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of Step 14. If the word כהונה does not teach 'right hand' for רבי שמעון, what is it doing in the פסוק about קבלה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about קבלה already says 'בני אהרן', which means כהנים. So the extra word 'הכהנים' must teach something. If it does not teach 'right hand' for רבי שמעון, the גמרא wants to know what it does teach.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest
Why do I need it? (asking what a word is there to teach)
Collecting the blood of a קרבן in a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not 'who may do קבלה'. Everyone agrees a כהן does it. The question is what the extra word adds.

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'priest'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 by asking what the extra word כהונה teaches if not the right hand.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 14's claim that for רבי שמעון, כהונה alone does not require the right hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every extra word in the תורה must teach something. If כהונה here does not teach right hand, it seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: The word כהן teaches that he must be in his priestly state
steps.stepSummary: The extra word teaches that the כהן must be in his כהונה, meaning wearing the priestly clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: In his priestly state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra word 'כהן' teaches a different law. The כהן must do קבלה while in his full priestly state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is not wasted, so it does not have to teach 'right hand'. It teaches that the כהן must be fully a כהן at that moment, wearing the בגדי כהונה. This keeps Step 14 standing.

keyTerms.meaning: In his priestly state (dressed as a כהן)
The priestly clothes

phrases.english: In his priestly state.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'in their priestly state' (round brackets); the corrected wording is 'in his' (square brackets). Either way, he means dressed in priestly clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by giving the extra word a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word כהן is useless unless it teaches right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word teaches that the כהן must be in his priestly state, so it does not have to teach right hand.

steps.title: זריקה only has כהונה, yet רבי שמעון does not argue that the left hand is פסול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that זריקה with the left hand is פסול, and רבי שמעון does not argue, even though only כהונה is written by זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at זריקה: only כהונה is written there, and we learned in the משנה: if he sprinkled with the left hand, it is פסול, and רבי שמעון does not argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to Step 14 from the משנה. By זריקה only כהונה is written, yet רבי שמעון seems to agree that the left hand is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון argues about קבלה with the left hand but stays quiet about זריקה. That silence suggests he agrees that זריקה needs the right hand. Since only כהונה is written by זריקה, it looks like כהונה alone does require the right hand for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח
Left (hand)
Invalid, disqualified
He argues, disagrees

phrases.english: But look at sprinkling,
where only priesthood is written about it;
and we learned: if he sprinkled with the left, it is invalid,
and Rabbi Shimon does not disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי זְרִיקָה דְּלָא כְּתִב בְּהוּ אֶלָּא כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 16 saved Step 14 from one question, this brings a new attack on Step 14 from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 14: for רבי שמעון, כהונה alone does not require the right hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's silence about זריקה in the משנה shows he agrees the left hand is פסול, even though only כהונה is written there.

steps.title: אביי: רבי שמעון does argue about זריקה in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון allows the left hand for both קבלה and זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He does argue, in a ברייתא. As it was taught: if he collected with the left, it is פסול, and רבי שמעון says it is כשר. If he sprinkled with the left, it is פסול, and רבי שמעון says it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the silence in the משנה proves nothing. A ברייתא openly records that רבי שמעון argues about זריקה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists both קבלה and זריקה, and by both רבי שמעון allows the left hand. So for him, כהונה alone does not require the right hand, just as Step 14 said. The משנה simply did not record his argument on זריקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not put into the משנה
Rules it valid (כשר)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, both קבלה and זריקה done with the left hand are כשר, because only כהונה is written there. He requires the right hand only where אצבע is written.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He disagrees in a baraita,
as it was taught: if he collected with the left, it is invalid,
and Rabbi Shimon rules it valid.
If he sprinkled with the left, it is invalid,
and Rabbi Shimon rules it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by bringing a ברייתא where רבי שמעון openly argues about זריקה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside source (ברייתא) that shows the opinion is recorded elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's silence in the משנה means he agrees זריקה needs the right hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: He argues in the ברייתא and allows the left hand for זריקה too, so Step 14 stands.

steps.title: Why does רבא need a word-link for קמיצה if רבה בר בר חנה's rule already covers it?
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns that קמיצה needs the right hand from a יד–יד link, but רבה בר בר חנה's rule should already teach that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רבא said: 'hand'–'hand' for קמיצה, 'foot'–'foot' for חליצה, 'ear'–'ear' for רציעה. Why do I need the first one? It already comes out from רבה בר בר חנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It quotes רבא's word-links and asks why the link for קמיצה is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of רבה בר בר חנה says that wherever אצבע or כהונה is written, the right hand is required. כהונה is written by קמיצה, so the right hand should already be required there. Then רבא's יד–יד link for קמיצה looks extra. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a handful from a מנחה
The ceremony of taking off the shoe of a brother-in-law who will not do יבום
Piercing the ear of an עבד עברי
It comes out, it is learned from

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבא (who made the word-links) with רבה בר בר חנה (who gave the right-hand rule). They are two different people.

phrases.english: But that which Rava said:
'Hand'–'hand' for taking the handful,
phrases.notes: The word 'hand' links the case back to the מצורע, so קמיצה is also done with the right hand.

phrases.english: 'foot'–'foot' for חליצה,
'ear'–'ear' for piercing;
why do I need it?
phrases.notes: This asks only about the first link, the one for קמיצה.

phrases.english: It comes out from Rabba bar bar Ḥana!
phrases.notes: His rule: where אצבע or כהונה is written, it means the right hand. כהונה is written by קמיצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the רבי שמעון line, the גמרא turns to a new problem: רבא's word-link seems unneeded because of רבה בר בר חנה's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כהונה is written by קמיצה, so רבה בר בר חנה's rule already requires the right hand there. A separate word-link would teach nothing new.

steps.title: One source for taking the handful, one for sanctifying it
steps.stepSummary: Both sources are needed. One teaches that taking the קומץ must be done with the right hand. The other teaches that putting the קומץ into a כלי שרת (קידוש קומץ) must also be done with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for taking the handful, and one is for sanctifying the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19: why do we need רבא's יד–יד link if רבה בר בר חנה's rule already teaches that קמיצה needs the right hand? It says each source covers a different act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 assumed both sources teach the same thing, so one of them would be extra. The answer is that there are two acts in the קומץ service: removing the handful from the מנחה, and then placing it into a second כלי שרת to make it holy. One source covers each act, so neither is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן takes out of a מנחה.
Making the handful holy by placing it into a כלי שרת.
One (Aramaic).

steps.whatToRemember: The right hand is needed both for taking the קומץ and for putting it into the כלי שרת. Each act has its own source, so both sources are needed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think קידוש קומץ is just another name for taking the handful. It is a separate act that comes after it: putting the handful into a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: One is for taking the handful,
and one is for sanctifying the handful.
phrases.notes: Sanctifying here means placing the handful into a second כלי שרת, and that needs the right hand too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by giving each source its own job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources between two separate acts (צריכותא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner assumed both sources teach the same right-hand rule for קמיצה, so one of them is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: One source makes the right hand required for taking the קומץ, and the other makes it required for קידוש קומץ in a כלי שרת.
